title: Patterning: The Dual of Interpretability
claim: Learned sensitivity directions pick out interpretable structure in training data, such as repeated rare terms that drive circuit formation.
layout: 1 panel, dense text block, per-token red-green highlighting
description: A single block of monospaced training-corpus text from a biomedical abstract about cytosolic phospholipase A2alpha in gene-targeted mice. Individual tokens carry colored background highlights. Red marks tokens with negative PC2 susceptibility values and green marks positive ones, and darker shades mean larger magnitude. The darkest red falls on rare biological terms such as 'phospholipase A2alpha', 'prostaglandins' and 'leukotrienes', and only from their second appearance onward. Common function words and mid-word fragments get faint green or pink shading. The text begins with '<|endoftext|>' markers. There are no arrows, axes or legends, so the eye goes first to the saturated red clusters on repeated technical terms.
caption: PC2 and induction patterns. Text from the training corpus highlighted in red and green based on PC2 value of the susceptibility vector of the 16 attention heads in the original model. Green indicates more positive values, while red indicates more negative. Note that the strongest red subsequences are rare biological terms, only highlighted red from their second appearance.
abstract: Mechanistic interpretability aims to understand how neural networks generalize beyond their training data by reverse-engineering their internal structures. We introduce patterning as the dual problem: given a desired form of generalization, determine what training data produces it. Our approach is based on susceptibilities, which measure how posterior expectation values of observables respond to infinitesimal shifts in the data distribution. Inverting this linear response relationship yields the data intervention that steers the model toward a target internal configuration. We demonstrate patterning in a small language model, showing that re-weighting training data along principal susceptibility directions can accelerate or delay the formation of structure, such as the induction circuit. In a synthetic parentheses balancing task where multiple algorithms achieve perfect training accuracy, we show that patterning can select which algorithm the model learns by targeting the local learning coefficient of each solution. These results establish that the same mathematical framework used to read internal structure can be inverted to write it.
